subject: Slotting Guidance: H100 vs A100 vs L4 for Dedicated Commitments
messages:
From: Simon Park <simon.park@orbitalai.com>

Date: 2027-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU guidance request (H100/A100/L4)

Hi Stephanie —

We are closing in on a Dedicated commitment and need a concise recommendation for GPU slotting. Our workload profile (attached) is: heavy conversational agents (~70% of tokens, average convo length ~2k tokens), high-frequency embeddings for search (30k reqs/day), and occasional long-context summarization jobs up to 32k tokens (batch offline).

Key concerns:
- Memory headroom for 32k summarization jobs
- Per-token economics for chat/embeddings
- Tail latency during peak bursts and a safe fallthrough strategy if reserve capacity hits limits

Can you advise how to think about H100 vs A100 vs L4 for a deal-sized commit (targeting predictable throughput with some burst)? We may have an initial 12-month reserved contract.

Attaching: orbital_workload_profile.csv

Thanks,
Simon Park
Director of ML Ops, OrbitalAI
[simon.park@orbitalai.com]

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU guidance request (H100/A100/L4)

Hi Simon —

Thanks for the profile — got it. Quick summary up-front so your procurement team has something to review:

- H100: best for long-context and peak latency-sensitive generation (32k jobs). Provides the largest model memory headroom and highest per-GPU throughput for large-context attention, but highest $/hour.
- A100: workhorse for balanced chat + embeddings workloads; good throughput and memory at a lower unit cost than H100.
- L4: optimized for high-concurrency, lower-cost inference (embeddings and short chat). Not suitable as the only SKU for 32k-context jobs.

My proposal: a tiered pool — primarily A100 for day-to-day chat+embeddings, reserve a smaller H100 pool sized for long-context and spike offload, and L4 slots for pure embedding-heavy endpoints to reduce unit cost. That preserves latency SLOs while optimizing cost.

I'll loop Ben (SE) to provide a sizing matrix and Dev (Ops) to note operational fallthroughs and contractual language for burst. Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to review?

Attachments: redwood_slotting_matrix.xlsx (initial draft)

Best,

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU guidance request (H100/A100/L4) — sizing matrix and calculations

Hi Simon —

I put together a compact sizing rationale based on the profile you shared. High-level numbers below (we can walk through the attached workbook):

Assumptions (from profile):
- Avg chat tokens / conversation: 2,000 tokens (largely streaming generation)
- Peak concurrent chats: 120
- Embedding QPS (peak): 350 qps
- Long-context summarization: 6 batch jobs/day, up to 32k tokens, typical batch size 8

Recommended slotting (starter commit) — capacity targets for predictable throughput:
- A100 slots: 28 slots (primary pool) — serves ~80% chat + majority of embeddings. Rationale: A100 80GB supports medium-long contexts, good cost/throughput.
- H100 slots: 6 slots (long-context pool + spike offload) — sized to accept 32k summarization jobs without disrupting chat SLOs.
- L4 slots: 10 slots (embedding-only endpoints and low-cost routing) — for high-concurrency embedding QPS at lowest marginal cost.

Operational headroom: +20% reserve (8 A100-equivalent slots) for canary/rollouts and burst. We recommend an autoscale burst policy that prefers L4 for embeddings and H100 only for real long-context runs.

Estimated economics (very rough):
- Tokens/sec per GPU (chat-heavy): A100 ~1400 tok/s, H100 ~2100 tok/s, L4 ~600 tok/s
- Cost per 1M tokens (approx): A100 ~$1.20, H100 ~$1.60, L4 ~$0.45 (varies with batching and caching)

Fallback policy suggestion:
1) If dedicated A100 pool saturated, route embedding traffic to L4 endpoints (preserve chat SLOs).
2) For long-context batch overflow, serialize or queue non-urgent jobs to off-peak windows or to a queued H100 worker pool.
3) Implement prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated token generation for chat contexts where applicable.

Attachments referenced: redwood_slotting_matrix.xlsx (detailed slot-per-workload tab), quick_calc_tokens_per_cost.csv (simple econ model).

Happy to present these numbers on the call and calibrate based on Orbital's internal SLAs.

Cheers,
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU guidance request (operational fallthrough & contract notes)

Simon —

Operational notes to make this contract safe and measurable:

Slot definition and SLOs:
- Define a "slot" by GPU SKU and concurrency profile (e.g., 1 A100 slot = 1 GPU with 6 max concurrent chat streams @2k avg tokens).
- Include a reserved headroom percentage (we recommend 20%) that is excluded from advertised throughput for maintenance/rollouts.

Burst / fallthrough mechanics:
- "Burst reserve": a smaller burst pool available for transient spikes (pay-for-burst add-on). If bursts exceed reserve, automatic fallback to lower-cost L4 for embedding endpoints and queued H100 for long jobs.
- Canaries & deployments: Dedicate 1–2 slots for canary traffic, never counted toward committed throughput.

Contractual language suggestions (short):
- Define measurable latency SLOs per endpoint class (chat, embedding, long-batch) and clear escalation paths.
- Include a "model-variant fallback" clause: Redwood can route to a compatible lower-memory model variant if the primary SKU pool is unavailable, with a specified latency and quality degradation profile.

Telemetry & chargeback:
- We will provide per-route token-by-token cost traces and per-slot utilization dashboards. Agreeing on a monthly cadence for utilization review helps avoid overcommit.

Let us know if procurement wants explicit language; we can draft a short appendix for the Master Services Agreement.

—Dev
